summary: Saudi Arabia offers citizens of 68 countries a one-year multiple-entry tourist eVisa (with mandatory medical insurance bundled into the fee) allowing stays of up to 90 days, gives the same group and holders of valid US, UK or Schengen visas a visa on arrival, and routes everyone else through embassy visas or the separate Hajj and Umrah regimes.

notes: The UK FCDO lists alcohol, pork and pork products, pornographic material, distillery equipment, weapons and narcotics among the items it is illegal to import. Do not bring alcohol, including duty-free.

The UK FCDO says some prescribed and over-the-counter medicines are controlled substances in Saudi Arabia and may need approval from the Saudi authorities. Carry an official prescription or a doctor’s letter stating the drug, dosage and amount.

There is zero tolerance for drug offences: the UK FCDO says possessing even small amounts can bring up to 5 years in prison and a 30,000 riyal fine, and dealing or smuggling can result in a death sentence.

safety.text: Since 13 July 2026 Houthi missiles and drones have targeted cities, airports and energy sites across Saudi Arabia, including Riyadh, Jeddah, Abha and Jizan, the FCDO reports. It advises against all travel within 10 km of the Yemen border and all but essential travel up to 80 km from it, now including Abha and Khamis Mushait. Follow Saudi Civil Defence alerts. Street crime is low; laws on drugs, alcohol and public behavior are strict.

tips.text: Do not bring alcohol into Saudi Arabia or arrive under its influence. The UK FCDO says it is illegal to drink alcohol or be drunk in public, and that brewing, possessing or selling alcohol can bring severe penalties, including prison.

The UK FCDO says men and women must wear loose-fitting clothing that covers the elbows and goes below the knees, avoiding profane or political slogans. Female travellers do not have to wear an abaya or cover their hair.

During Ramadan the UK FCDO says not to eat, drink, smoke or chew gum in public in the daytime, including in your car, and not to play loud music or dance. Check the opening hours of shops and restaurants.
Women aged 18+ can now visit Saudi Arabia independently. No male guardian or male travel companion is required for tourist entry.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Saudi Arabia?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders need a tourist eVisa (applied for at visa.visitsaudi.com) or a visa on arrival at major airports. Both cost SAR 395 including mandatory medical insurance and give a one-year, multiple-entry visa with stays of up to 90 days.

faq.question: How much does the Saudi tourist eVisa cost?
faq.answer: SAR 395 (about USD 105), which includes the application fee and the compulsory medical insurance. If you qualify only through a US, UK or Schengen visa or residence permit, the eVisa costs SAR 339.44 and you buy the insurance separately. Apply only on the official portal visa.visitsaudi.com.

faq.question: Can I get a Saudi visa on arrival with a US, UK or Schengen visa?
faq.answer: Yes. Holders of a valid US, UK or Schengen tourist or business visa that has been used at least once (with an entry stamp from the issuing country — digital stamps are not accepted), and holders of a UK, US or EU permanent residence permit, are eligible for a visa on arrival whether or not their nationality is on the eVisa list — a route often used by Indian, Pakistani and Filipino travelers. Confirm current conditions on visa.visitsaudi.com before flying.

faq.question: Can I perform Umrah on a tourist eVisa, and what vaccinations do pilgrims need?
faq.answer: Yes — tourist eVisa holders may perform Umrah (outside the Hajj season). Hajj requires a separate Hajj visa issued through official quota channels. All pilgrims must carry a valid quadrivalent meningococcal ACWY vaccination certificate, issued at least 10 days before arrival, and seasonal extra requirements can apply depending on your departure country.

faq.question: Is alcohol allowed in Saudi Arabia?
faq.answer: No. The UK FCDO lists alcohol among the items it is illegal to import and advises not bringing any, including duty-free. It is illegal to drink alcohol or be drunk in public, and brewing, possessing or selling alcohol can bring severe penalties, including prison.
